items.prompt: Where did Bayu find the map?

options.text: under the stone with the white stripe
options.why: That is where the biscuit tin was hidden.

options.text: in a rusty biscuit tin
options.why: The tin was found later, by following the map.

options.text: inside an old exercise book in Nenek’s wooden chest
in one of Nenek’s photo albums
options.why: They were looking for the albums, but the map was in an exercise book.

hints: The answer is in the first paragraph.
Look for the words The map was folded.
Read to the end of the first sentence.
items.explanation: The first sentence says the map was folded inside an old exercise book at the bottom of Nenek’s wooden chest.

items.prompt: Read: “It’s probably a joke,” I said. But I was already reaching for my sandals. What does this show about Laila?

options.text: She says she doubts the map, but she really wants to search.
She thinks the map is funny.
options.why: She calls it a joke, but her actions show she takes it seriously.

options.text: She wants to go home.
options.why: She is reaching for her sandals to go out searching.

options.text: She is angry with Bayu.
options.why: Nothing in these lines shows anger.

hints: Compare what Laila says with what she does.
The word But shows that her actions do not match her words.
Ask: why would she reach for her sandals if she thought it was only a joke?
items.explanation: Laila says the map is probably a joke, but she is already getting ready to go out. Her actions show she is curious and wants to search.

items.prompt: Why do you think Nenek put on her best kebaya before she dialled Tuti’s number?

options.text: She was going to a party that evening.
options.why: The story does not mention a party.

options.text: Tuti had asked her to dress smartly.
options.why: Tuti could not see her on the phone and had not asked anything.

options.text: She was more excited about speaking to Tuti than she wanted to admit.
She always wore it when she shelled peanuts.
options.why: She put it on specially, just before she dialled.

hints: Look at what Nenek says and what she does in the last paragraph.
Her words and her actions do not match.
Ask: why would someone dress up for an important phone call?
items.explanation: Nenek says it is silly to get excited, but she dresses up and keeps the photograph on her lap. Her actions show how much the call means to her.

items.prompt: Why was the colonial government furious with Soewardi in 1913?

options.text: His article publicly criticised the government.
He refused to finish his medical training.
options.why: He left his course because of illness.

options.text: He opened a school without permission.
options.why: Taman Siswa opened in 1922, years later.

options.text: He changed his name.
options.why: He changed his name much later.

hints: Find the year 1913 in the text.
Read what he wrote and what it said about the government.
Ask: how would rulers feel about being criticised in public?
items.explanation: His article “If I Were a Dutchman” criticised the colonial government, which made the government furious.

items.prompt: Which group of people worries that customers will shop somewhere else?
hints: This information is in the part of the text that gives arguments against the idea.
Look for the paragraph that begins However.
Find the word customers.
items.explanation: The text says that some shop owners on Jalan Merdeka worry that customers will not be able to park and will shop elsewhere.

Africa
options.why: Africa is not mentioned in the text.

options.text: Australia
Europe
options.why: Europe is not mentioned in the text.

options.text: South America
options.why: South America is not mentioned in the text.

hints: Look for the words two huge areas of land.
One is to the north and one is to the south.
Read the first sentence of the third paragraph.
items.explanation: The text says Indonesia lies between Asia to the north and Australia to the south.

items.prompt: Why does the west monsoon bring heavy rain to Java?

options.text: The wind blows from the dry land of Australia.
options.why: That describes the east monsoon, which brings the dry season.

options.text: The wind picks up water vapour over warm seas, and the moist air rises and cools into clouds.
The sea heats up faster than the land.
options.why: The text says the opposite: land heats up faster.

options.text: Farmers plant rice, which makes clouds form.
options.why: Planting rice depends on the rain. It does not cause it.

hints: Find the paragraph about December to February.
Follow the wind’s journey: where does it travel over, and what does it pick up?
Look for what happens when the moist air reaches the islands.
items.explanation: The wind crosses warm seas and picks up water vapour. Over Indonesia the moist air rises, cools and condenses, so heavy rain falls.

items.prompt: In Poem A, what does Father say they will do tomorrow?
hints: Look at the last line of Poem A.
Find the word Father.
Read what comes after Father says.
items.explanation: The last line says: Tomorrow, Father says, we plant. Now that the rain has come, the fields can be planted.

items.prompt: Find and copy one word that means tied up in one place. Look in the paragraph that begins The boat, called Pustaka Laut.
hints: Read the paragraph about the boat slowly.
The word describes what the boat does at each island.
Look at the sentence that begins Every two weeks.
items.explanation: Moored means tied up so that a boat stays in one place. The boat spends a day moored at each island.

items.prompt: Choose 2 challenges that the project faces.

options.text: Rough seas can make the crossing unsafe.
Children do not want to borrow books.
options.why: The children wait on the jetty, waving.

options.text: Books can be damaged by sea spray and damp air.
The boat is too small for 2,000 books.
options.why: The report does not say this.

options.text: Teachers do not like the visits.
options.why: Ibu Rahmi says the visits are making a difference.

hints: Look for the paragraph that begins However.
However often introduces problems after good news.
Find the two sentences that describe problems.
items.explanation: The report says rough seas sometimes make the crossing unsafe and books can be damaged by spray and damp.
